August 30, 2026

Israeli settlers attack NBC News crew in occupied West Bank

tags: media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

An NBC News team was assaulted by Israeli settlers near the town of Jaloud in the occupied West Bank while interviewing a Palestinian woman, who was also attacked. At least one masked settler carrying a club struck the crew; correspondent Matt Bradley said the assailants jumped out, beat them, and drove off. Reports indicated as many as five NBC journalists were injured, though all injuries were described as non-life-threatening and those hurt were treated. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned the attack, as did members of Congress and other US officials.

Trump refers NBC's Kristen Welker to the FCC over her comments on his endorsements

tags: media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump said he is referring Meet the Press host Kristen Welker to the Federal Communications Commission for what he called purposeful inaccuracy, after she said his candidate endorsements have had mixed results. A number of candidates he endorsed have lost their races. Trump went on to call for the FCC to act against what he described as crooked media and fake polls. The FCC is designed as an independent regulator of US communications.

Russian threats against UK bases and Polish warnings raise fears of NATO escalation

tags: war, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A spokeswoman for Russia's foreign ministry said Russia could begin striking military bases in the United Kingdom. Separately, Poland's Donald Tusk said Russian aggression tied to the war in Ukraine is growing and that the next six months will be decisive, adding that Poland and NATO are preparing for a range of scenarios. The statements follow CIA Director John Ratcliffe's visit to Russia, the first such trip in five years, and warnings from foreign leaders who say they have intelligence pointing to Russian escalation against a NATO member.

Tucker Carlson calls for Trump's impeachment and removal over Iran nuclear talk

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas

Tucker Carlson, previously a supporter of the president, is calling for Trump's immediate impeachment and removal from office. Carlson tied the call to discussions about the possibility that Trump could use a nuclear weapon in Iran, a claim that has not been confirmed. The move adds Carlson to a list of former backers who now say the president should be removed rather than simply withdrawing their support.

Federal appeals court rules AI-generated child sexual abuse imagery is protected speech

tags: legal, tech
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A federal appeals court panel in the Seventh Circuit ruled that private possession of entirely AI-generated child exploitation material is protected by the First Amendment, provided no real children are depicted. The judges said they were bound by earlier Supreme Court precedent, including a 2002 decision. The ruling is expected to be appealed to the Supreme Court, and is being cited as an argument for regulation of AI-generated content.

DHS whistleblowers say ICE is preparing voter fraud operations in blue states before midterms

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Whistleblowers inside the Department of Homeland Security say ICE's Homeland Security Investigations unit is preparing a large push targeting voter fraud in blue states and sanctuary cities ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, with operations already underway in some areas. The claim follows a DHS request for information issued on 25 August 2026 seeking voter registration files and voting history data from all 50 states. DHS said the data would be used by HSI for fraud detection and data segmentation.

White House said to be testing limits of secrecy laws ahead of possible investigations

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

CNN has reported that the White House is preparing for large-scale investigations should Democrats take control of the House or Senate, and is examining how far secrecy laws can be stretched to keep material private. The effort is said to cover the president, his children, his wife, and staff. Financial records are among the material the administration wants to keep from Congress, the courts, and the public.

Brennan Center confirms 56 pre-written presidential emergency documents

tags: politics, surveillance
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The Brennan Center for Justice has confirmed the existence of 56 Presidential Emergency Action Documents, pre-written executive orders, proclamations, and messages to Congress prepared in advance for emergency situations. The documents themselves are classified, but the subjects they cover have been confirmed. They include authorized detention of alien enemies and other dangerous persons, suspension of habeas corpus, forms of martial law, general warrants for search and seizure, establishment of military areas, suspension of the Federal Register, a declared state of war, and authorized censorship of news reports.

Project 2025 tracker shows roughly half of planned actions completed

tags: politics, immigration, health
sources: @total.hypocrisy

A Heritage Foundation fundraising email sent in February said 283 of 532 tracked Project 2025 actions had been completed. Remaining items include an FDA move against mifepristone approval, restrictions on obtaining abortion pills via telehealth or across state lines, and use of a 150-year-old anti-obscenity law to prosecute the mailing of abortion pills without congressional action. Other planned steps cover full elimination of the Department of Education, folding the FBI's in-house legal function under the Justice Department, rollbacks of fuel efficiency and air pollution rules, federal override of state blocks on energy projects, and reduced protections for public lands and wildlife. On immigration, the agenda includes nationwide mandatory E-Verify, mandatory detention during proceedings, cuts to sanctuary city funding, removal of domestic and gang violence as asylum grounds, narrowed parole, and a durable Remain in Mexico policy, funded by the ICE allocation signed into law in July 2025 that begins in 2027.

Trump moves to loosen beef processing rules, alarming food safety advocates

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump pledged over the past 24 hours to allow farmers and ranchers to process their own meat, a step aimed at the market power of the four dominant meat packers: Tyson, Cargill, JBS, and National Beef. Food safety advocates say the change could worsen food-borne illness, which is already rising in the United States, and argue the federal restrictions being relaxed are necessary to protect the beef supply. A related House bill that would have allowed meat from small custom slaughterhouses to be sold in-state without federal inspection did not pass.

Trump cabinet secretaries confronted by voters on the campaign trail

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Cabinet members sent out across the country by Trump and Susie Wiles to promote the administration's economic message have been repeatedly confronted by voters, according to Politico. Energy Secretary Chris Wright faced complaints about gas prices, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins was questioned in Iowa about beef prices and the origin of imported beef, and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was challenged over an ongoing measles outbreak in Florida. The tour was intended to lift the president's favorability numbers.

Google Maps renames Lake Ontario as Lake America for US users

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

Google Maps changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America for users in the United States overnight, following the US Geological Survey's official change. Apple Maps has not made the change and MapQuest said it will not, prompting anger on the right and calls from some in MAGA for a boycott of Apple Maps. The renaming applies only within the United States; users in Canada and elsewhere still see Lake Ontario. Trump also posted an AI-generated video of a duck with his hairstyle carrying firearms, captioned as Lake America being protected by Donald Dux.

White House insiders say Trump is prioritising his legacy over Republican midterm wins

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A Daily Beast report says White House insiders are concerned for the first time that Trump is focused on protecting his legacy, family, and businesses rather than on Republicans winning in November. Republicans including Stephanie Bice, in a district Trump carried by nine points, have expressed concern that he is focused on matters such as renaming a lake rather than lowering costs. The worry inside the White House and in Congress is framed around what happens if Democrats take the House or Senate in January.

Florida operation recovers 163 children in largest such effort in state history

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A multi-day law enforcement operation in Florida called Operation Statewide Shield located 163 children ranging in age from two months to 17 years, according to the Florida Attorney General. Recoveries by region included 46 in Tampa Bay, 41 in Miami, 32 in Jacksonville, 21 in Orlando, 12 in Fort Myers, eight in Pensacola, and three in Tallahassee. Some of the children showed evidence of abuse, neglect, and criminal activity including human trafficking. Arrests were made as part of the operation.
